Amid attacks, sales surge at Kolkata Left bookstalls
articles.summary: Book stalls set up by Left parties saw significant sales increases during Durga Puja amid incidents of vandalism. The CPM stall at Jadavpur 8B bus stand recorded sales of Rs 16 lakh, nearly four times last year's figures. Despite attacks, sales for other Left stalls also increased, evidencing a broader engagement with literature. Politicians from various parties expressed solidarity with the Left stalls amidst ongoing disputes.

articles.title: Anahat scripts history, storms into maiden PSA Gold semi-final
articles.summary: Anahat Singh pulled off an impressive comeback against Salma Hany, clinching her spot in the semi-finals at a PSA Gold-level event after a nail-biting five-game match that lasted 42 minutes. The 18-year-old, facing a 1-2 deficit, demonstrated resilience and skill. Anahat will now go head-to-head with Malaysia's Sivasangari Subramaniam, reigniting their rivalry from the Asian Games final, solidifying her remarkable tournament journey in Redwood City.

articles.title: Florida cop accused of stealing dead man's home, spending $214K
articles.summary: Florida police officer Brian Louis Sguros is accused of taking over 71-year-old Dennis West’s home weeks after finding him dead in 2022. Authorities allege Sguros impersonated West and spent more than $214,000 renovating the property. He was arrested on multiple felony charges and placed on unpaid administrative leave as the case proceeds through court.

articles.title: Judi Dench, 91, says she can no longer see to act or read
articles.summary: Judi Dench, 91, has revealed that deteriorating eyesight has left her unable to act on stage, make films or read. Speaking on BBC Radio 4’s Today programme, the Oscar winner said she could no longer recognise faces clearly and had missed seeing bluebells this summer. Diagnosed with age-related macular degeneration in 2012, Dench continues to face daily challenges.

articles.title: 56-year-old Utah grandmother delivers grandson as surrogate
articles.summary: A Utah woman diagnosed with rare uterine sarcoma at 25 lost her uterus, leaving her unable to carry a pregnancy. Her 56-year-old mother-in-law, Jessie Boren, volunteered to become a gestational surrogate for her and her husband. After two embryo transfers, Jessie delivered their baby boy via C-section three months ago, turning their difficult journey into a hopeful new beginning.

articles.title: Congress defaming India to shield Nehru-Gandhi family: PM Modi
articles.summary: “Dimagi naxals have captured Congress so much that it has lost its ability to think. articles.title: 'He put it back': Trump says Ukraine's Starlink restored, stays silent on Musk
articles.summary: Ukraine depends heavily on Starlink for communications between military units, coordinating operations and receiving early warnings during Russian missile attacks. The satellite-based network also supports the use of drones, which Ukraine deploys both to strike Russian targets and to defend against incoming attacks. Disruptions to connectivity can therefore affect the military's ability to operate drones and respond to Russian assaults.

articles.title: Tom Brady donated $170,000 Salem State speaking fee to charities in 2015
articles.summary: Tom Brady collected $170,000 for a speaking gig at Salem State University, generously donating the entire sum to charity. He allocated $50,000 to Best Buddies and distributed the remaining funds to various other organizations. With approximately 4,000 attendees present, ticket sales effectively covered his speaking fee. However, the event was notable for Brady facing questions about the NFL's Deflategate saga. The university reported a financial profit from hosting the event.

articles.title: When mob takes law into its own hands: another man lynched in Keralam’s Palakkad

Shiva Shanker

Four of the tankers reportedly caught fire while transferring oil, creating significant challenges. Iranian authorities have warned of potential targeting of US bases if the situation escalates.

articles.title: Asian Para Games: Where India stands in medal tally after best day with 7 golds
articles.summary: India showcased an extraordinary performance at the Asian Para Games 2026, clinching 26 medals and securing a commendable fourth place overall. With a breathtaking total of 88 medals, including 21 gold, the day was especially memorable for armless archer Sheetal Devi, who bagged two golds in quick succession. Para-athletics was pivotal in this achievement, propelling India past South Korea in the medal standings.

articles.title: Marine life on the brink? 96% of coral reefs could face collapse by 2075
articles.summary: The International Union for Conservation of Nature recently highlighted the alarming vulnerability of coral reefs, predicting that by 2075, nearly all shallow-water coral systems may collapse due to rising ocean temperatures. This impending crisis threatens not only marine biodiversity but also the local communities that depend on these ecosystems for their livelihoods.

articles.title: Connecticut wool mill that lost 85 jobs now employs 50, makes military fabric
articles.summary: A Connecticut wool mill that closed in 2013, leaving 85 workers jobless, has been revived by former investment banker Jacob Harrison Long. He bought the 475,000-square-foot factory in 2014 despite having no manufacturing experience. Twelve years later, the mill employs about 50 people and supplies fabric for US military uniforms. Long now hopes to expand textile manufacturing across New England.

articles.title: Newton's 1687 book on gravity, funded by Halley, sold for Rs 5.49 crore
articles.summary: In a significant auction event, a first edition of Isaac Newton's *Philosophiæ naturalis principia mathematica* garnered an impressive US$576,000. This pivotal work introduced revolutionary concepts of motion and gravity through mathematical frameworks. With ties to distinguished scholars like the Kennet family and the vital endorsement from Edmond Halley, Newton's insights continue to resonate in disciplines such as engineering and astronomy, shaping modern scientific thought.

articles.title: Minnesota court reverses $20,000 privacy award in driveway camera feud
articles.summary: In Minnesota, a conflict brewed between two couples over a shared driveway and the removal of a tree. The Stahleys performed maintenance on the Rubys' land without consent, leading to a legal battle. Ultimately, the court awarded the Rubys $27,000, with $20,000 for invasion of privacy. However, the appeals court overturned the privacy ruling, necessitating further proceedings and adjusting the damages for tree removal.

articles.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo reportedly invested $70 million in real estate in 2025
articles.summary: Since October 2025, NBA superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo has strategically invested approximately $70 million in various real estate ventures. His family's company, Ante, has facilitated several significant purchases, including apartment complexes in Wisconsin, Brooklyn, and Chicago. Notably, he recently acquired a lavish $13.5 million mansion in Pinecrest, Florida, after joining the Miami Heat. These investments reflect Antetokounmpo's commitment to expanding his financial portfolio beyond basketball income.

articles.title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes' soccer club value jumps from $275M to $325M

The growth in value reflects the stability of the league and solid revenue generation capabilities. Meanwhile, the club continues to work on improving its on-field performance after winning the 2025 Shield.

articles.title: Maldives begins planting coral on 2 submerged planes to build artificial reef
articles.summary: Two decommissioned Dornier 228 aircraft are submerged near Kudagiri Island to create a diving attraction. Conservation teams are working to establish an artificial reef by attaching coral fragments to underwater frames. The project aims to combine marine tourism with aviation history while promoting coral growth. Various organizations are collaborating to monitor the ecological impact of this initiative.

Other companies are emerging as competitors, offering alternative drone solutions by 2029. This shift reflects ongoing discussions on military procurement and strategic autonomy amid increasing global security concerns.

articles.title: Ralf Schumacher says Lewis Hamilton and Fernando Alonso block young F1 drivers

articles.title: Frankfurt’s fitted kitchens turn 100; volunteers save parts from about 50
articles.summary: In the year 1926, Margarete Schütte-Lihotzky revolutionized domestic design by creating the Frankfurt Kitchen, aimed at maximizing cooking efficiency for urban dwellers. While around 10,000 of these iconic kitchens were initially integrated into Frankfurt residences, many have since succumbed to renovations. Today, preservationists are dedicated to conserving the remaining kitchens, adapting them with modern appliances while respecting their historical integrity.

articles.title: Why some couples are comfortable with silence, according to psychology
articles.summary: Silence in romantic relationships can signal comfort or discomfort based on personal communication styles and emotional needs. The 2024 study revealed that chosen silence often indicates emotional security and closeness. Alternatively, silence resulting from anxiety or hostility may lead to misunderstandings and emotional distance. Understanding each other's preferences regarding conversation and quiet time can strengthen relationships. Ultimately, intimacy is shaped by both meaningful conversations and moments of peaceful silence.

articles.title: Rare 1896 Chaucer book with 87 woodcuts sold for Rs 2.68 crore

With only about 50 deluxe copies ever bound, this book's rarity and artistic illustrations by Edward Burne-Jones continue to captivate collectors, emphasizing the allure of beautifully crafted literary works.

articles.title: Why some people struggle to say no even when exhausted, according to psychology

This habit stems from a fear of disappointing others, which can make saying no feel uncomfortable. Continued agreement may cause emotional exhaustion and hinder personal relationships. Effective strategies for setting boundaries include pausing before answering requests and practicing refusal in low-pressure situations.

Google CEO Sundar Pichai reportedly declined his proposal on the grounds that oceans encompass multiple countries. This follows the US administration's earlier renaming of Lake Ontario to Lake America for US users.

articles.title: Facial laser session leaves woman with burns; consumer panel orders Rs 1.11 lakh payout
articles.summary: In an alarming incident at Berkowits Hair & Skin Clinic in Bengaluru, a woman suffered severe second-degree burns during a laser hair removal treatment. Despite her intense pain, the technician minimized her discomfort, labeling it as normal. Subsequent medical examinations validated her injuries. The district consumer commission held the clinic accountable for inadequate service and mandated compensation, including a refund and damages for her injuries and emotional distress.

Overall revenue increased to $64.60 billion, primarily driven by higher advertising earnings. However, operating income declined due to a significant legal charge linked to teen mental health litigation. The company plans to invest heavily in artificial intelligence infrastructure to support future revenue growth.

articles.title: Paid Rs 1 lakh for gold chain, got nothing; jeweller ordered to pay Rs 1.3 lakh
articles.summary: Himachal Pradesh state consumer commission upheld a decision directing Shri Ganesh Jewellers to refund Rs 1 lakh. Customer M R Chauhan made an advance payment for a gold chain that was never delivered. Despite repeated requests and a police complaint, the jeweller failed to return the money. The commission awarded compensation of Rs 20,000 for mental harassment and Rs 10,000 for litigation costs.

articles.title: US soldier killed at 17 in Korean War identified after 75 years, to be buried
articles.summary: Pvt. Joseph E. Boyd, who went missing in action at just 17 during the Korean War, has finally been identified decades later. His remains, previously known as Unknown X-1642, have been matched to his identity through advanced forensic techniques, including DNA testing. A dignified burial ceremony is set for October 21, 2026, in Owings Mills, Maryland, underscoring the ongoing commitment to honor missing service members from historical conflicts.

articles.title: Virginia teen's model improves simulated earthquake sensor coverage by 16.7%
articles.summary: A 14-year-old student from Williamsburg, Virginia, has become one of 30 finalists in a national science competition after developing a mathematical model to improve earthquake sensor placement. Isabel Rossi's six-month research project showed that adding just five sensors could increase simulated detection coverage by 16.7%. She used earthquake records from California and mathematical methods to identify better sensor locations.

articles.title: United Airlines CEO says Starlink is helping win customers; Musk responds
articles.summary: This week, United Airlines aims to have Starlink on more than half of its flights, looking to fully implement the service across its fleet by the end of the following year. CEO Scott Kirby believes this partnership offers a distinct edge in attracting new passengers, especially as rising fuel costs weigh on profits amidst ongoing geopolitical issues.

articles.title: Texas man, 86, spends 39 years building 62-foot boat; strangers step in
articles.summary: An 86-year-old man from Mineral Wells, Texas, has been building a 62-foot steel boat since 1987. After three visitors discovered his ambition, they launched a crowdfunding campaign to support the project. More than $41,000 has been raised towards completing the boat and moving it to a launch site. The remaining work on the vessel is expected to require about $50,000 in funding.

articles.title: 'Am studying his body': Trump goes into graphic detail about US senator's body at rally
Viral fever, vomiting: How Praveen Kumar fought back to win Asian Para Games gold
articles.summary: Praveen Kumar won the men’s high jump T44/64 gold medal at the Asian Para Games in Japan. He accomplished this while dealing with a hip injury and battling fever, cold, and cough. Despite these challenges, he cleared 2.05m, setting a new Games record. His previous record was 1.95m in the T44 category. Praveen aims to defend his Paralympic title at the next Los Angeles Games.

articles.title: 'Beacon of hope': Polish PM Tusk hails ties with India, calls PM Modi a 'friend'
articles.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk visited India to strengthen bilateral cooperation between India and Poland. He highlighted the absence of conflicts of interest and shared values between the two nations. Both leaders discussed expanding economic opportunities through the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement. Tusk emphasized the positive economic developments achieved by Poland and India over the last 35 years.

articles.title: Exhibition row: Raihan recounts how events unfolded before photos were taken down
articles.summary: Raihan Vadra's photography exhibition, No Idea Is Fine, allegedly faced turmoil at Bikaner House when management objected hours before its start, claiming venue policy violations. While Vadra proposed removing select images, the officials demanded the removal of all 70 photographs, including those depicting the Indian national flag. This sparked outrage among Congress members, igniting debates about censorship and the value of artistic freedom.

articles.title: Pala-era Vishnu sculpture sold for Rs 8.16 crore, over 9 times estimate
articles.summary: A blackstone sculpture of Vishnu, dating to the 11th or 12th century, sold for £635,000 at Christie’s auction. The sculpture was previously part of a Swiss collection and first sold in March 1973. Over the years, the artwork maintained its significance and desirability among collectors. In June 2026, it was auctioned again as part of a collection focusing on South Asian art.

articles.title: China's restored reefs hold 286 oysters per sq m; particles down 62%
articles.summary: A study of oyster reef restoration in China's Bohai Bay has found encouraging signs of marine habitat recovery between 2022 and 2026. By March 2026, artificial reefs supported an average of 286 oysters per square metre, while suspended particles in the water had declined by approximately 62%. Published in Frontiers in Marine Science, the study also recorded an increase in seabed animals. However, researchers said further monitoring was needed to establish the project's long-term effectiveness.

articles.title: Georgia woman loses marijuana smoke case as court upholds pension fund immunity
articles.summary: A Georgia woman sued after claiming her neighbour’s marijuana smoke repeatedly entered her apartment despite a no-smoking lease, affecting her breathing and health. Bridget Francis alleged that the apartment management ignored her complaints. However, on October 19, 2026, a Georgia appeals court upheld the dismissal of her claims against a California teachers’ pension fund, ruling that it was legally protected from the lawsuit.

articles.title: Delhi-NCR pollution: How GRAP Stage 1 curbs can protect your heart and lungs
articles.summary: Delhi-NCR has launched GRAP Stage 1 to combat the rising air pollution levels and protect health standards. The initiative focuses on controlling dust, limiting specific fuel types, and tightening regulatory enforcement. Health experts stress the importance of immediate intervention to guard vulnerable populations against the health implications of poor air quality. Citizens are urged to adopt personal safety measures during smoggy days.

articles.title: 'Vidhan Sabha uda diya': Bengaluru police arrest Bihar man over AI video

The video depicted a bomb blast at Vidhana Soudha, the Karnataka government's seat. The suspect, Hazrat Ali Shoiab, had been working as a daily-wage pipefitter in the city. Police discovered the footage during routine digital surveillance and tracked down the suspect's account. Investigations are ongoing to understand Shoiab's motives and identify any collaborators.

articles.title: ‘It was scripted, a joke’: Delhi influencer apologises over racial abuse of Tripura youth

After the incident, Bhadauriya was taken to Lala Lajpat Rai Hospital where he later died.

Tesla's revenue was flat compared to the previous year but still surpassed estimates, while net income fell 43%. Demand for electric vehicles rose significantly as Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the quarter.

articles.title: Sheetal Devi, Toman Kumar win compound mixed team gold at Asian Para Games

The Indian pair defeated Indonesia’s Teodora Audi Ayudia Ferelly and Ken Swagumilang 151-148 in the final. The top-seeded Indian team stayed ahead for most of the contest and held on to win by three points.

articles.title: Was Tiger Shroff the real target? | Pulse Maharashtra
articles.summary:
A celebrity shootout in Mumbai has sent shockwaves through the financial capital and has spread fear in the Hindi film industry. This wasn’t the first shootout in the city this year. And now, the industry is scared of the dark shadows of the past, when the underworld called the shots in Bollywood. And just like the past, this time too, the masterminds seem to be operating from foreign shores. But was Tiger Shroff the real target? Is this shootout related to incidents like the firing outside actor Salman Khan’s residence, the murder of NCP leader Baba Siddique, the shooting outside filmmaker Rohit Shetty’s residence and the reported threats to actors Ranveer Singh and Aamir Khan?

In this week’s Pulse Maharashtra with Vinaya Deshpande, we take you through what we know so far and what the unanswered questions are. And how this attack leads to an old fear in the heart of an industry which is one of India’s greatest soft powers in the world – Bollywood.

articles.title: CJP leaders released after court rejects police plea for extended custody
articles.summary:
After spending seven days in jail, Cockroach Janta Party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka have been released following an order by a Special Executive Magistrate court in Delhi.

The two leaders were detained after the October 13 protest at Jantar Mantar and had been held in judicial custody while police sought preventive action against them. The court eventually ordered their release after they submitted undertakings promising not to organise protests at Jantar Mantar while the site remains denotified and not to disturb public peace.

articles.summary: A French Mirage 2000D fighter jet crashed while returning to its air base after a night training mission. The justice department accused Instacart of creating burdens for U.S. applicants during the Permanent Labor Certification process. A settlement has been reached, requiring Instacart to establish a fund for affected applicants and pay civil penalties. articles.summary: In a notable case from Missouri, a couple gained legal rights to their isolated property via their neighbor's land. Although the court initially granted them ownership of the access road, it later corrected this decision. Ultimately, they received a permanent easement, illustrating the difference between property rights and ownership. The couple can access their property while the neighbor retains the land under the road.

articles.title: Meloni toughens Italy protest laws: Teen detentions, parental liability, 5-year jail

Authorities now have increased powers to detain youths perceived as threats, irrespective of actual criminal acts.

articles.title: Crude could hit $140 in early 2027 if Gulf supply disruptions persist: Goldman Sachs
articles.summary: Commodity prices are expected to experience volatility due to geopolitical conflicts and supply chain disruptions. Energy prices may rise sharply if Middle Eastern supplies remain constrained or degrade further. Agricultural markets could face pressure from various conflicts and potential weather disruptions linked to El Niño. Satisfied with his innings, especially after a rough patch, Bavuma also credited Marco Jansen and Simon Harmer for their support, urging bowlers to elevate their game as well.

articles.title: Margot Robbie's $950,000 Hollywood bungalow later sold for about $1.2m

She eventually sold the property in 2021 for around $1.2 million, marking a profitable investment. Despite the ocean separating him from Lanka, Lord Ram mobilised collective strength, brought together available resources and achieved what appeared impossible, he said. “We must not sit relying on others. We must recognise our own strength and we must have faith in our own resources,” the PM said, linking the message to the goals of ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’ and ‘Viksit Bharat’.

articles.title: Hacker group claims access to 3.8 lakh SBI data entries

articles.title: Smartphone shipments slip, Chinese brands lose ground
